summary: A step-by-step tutorial by Adam Bertram (article written by Michael Soule) on building an AWS Lambda PowerShell function that provisions IAM roles from configuration templates stored in an S3 bucket. It covers prerequisites, creating the S3 bucket with public access blocked, creating an IAM role and policies, writing and publishing the Lambda script, configuring an hourly CloudWatch Events trigger, uploading test role JSON files, and manually invoking the function to verify the role was created.
one_line: Tutorial on building an AWS Lambda PowerShell function that reads IAM role templates from S3 and creates IAM roles automatically.
key_facts: The tutorial was published on January 14, 2021 on the Adam the Automator (ATA) blog and was written by Michael Soule, a frequent contributor, with Adam Bertram credited as the blog author.

Prerequisites include PowerShell Core 6.0, .NET Core 2.1 SDK, the AWSPowerShell.NetCore 4.0.1.1 and AWSLambdaPSCore 1.2.0.0 PowerShell modules, and an AWS CLI profile with the default region set to us-east-1.
The example S3 bucket is named awslambdapowershelldemo1, and S3 bucket names must be globally unique and lowercase.
The S3 bucket is created with public access block settings set to true for BlockPublicAcl, BlockPublicPolicy, IgnorePublicAcl and RestrictPublicBucket.
The IAM role created for the Lambda function is named ROLE-RoleManager and its trust policy allows the lambda.amazonaws.com service to assume it.
The inline policy POLICY-ROLE-RoleManager is written to ROLE-RoleManager, and the AWS managed policy arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole is registered to it.
The example custom policy allows any IAM action against any resource, and the article advises limiting actions and resources in a production deployment.
The Lambda script is named FUNCTION-RoleManager-1.ps1 and is created with the New-AWSPowerShellLambda cmdlet using the Basic template.
The Lambda function is published with the Publish-AWSPowerShellLambda cmdlet, which zips the script and uploads it to the AWS Lambda service.
The CloudWatch Event rule is named RULE-CronHourly and uses the schedule expression rate(1 hour) with state ENABLED.

The Lambda function reads object keys in the form ACCOUNT-OR-SERVICE/ROLE-NAME/POLICY-NAME.json, where a 12-digit entity is treated as an AWS account number and any other entity is treated as an AWS service name.
Files named managed.json contain a list of AWS managed policy ARNs under the key arn, and other JSON files are attached as inline customer managed policies named after the file.
The test role example uses the managed policy arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess and an inline policy file named POLICY-FullAdmin.json under the ROLE-Name role.
The function is manually invoked with Invoke-LMFunction, and the new role is verified with Get-IAMRole -RoleName ROLE-Name.
The full code is available in a GitHub repository at Snozzberries/AWS-Role-Manager.
